results.name: Parcel_Boundaries_of_Indiana_Current
results.title: Parcel Boundaries of Indiana Current
results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. These layers include address points, street centerlines, land parcels, and governmental boundaries.
results.snippet:
This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

If attempting to download this data in shapefile or file geodatabase format on indianamap.org, please note that this dataset is too large to fit in a shapefile and generating a geodatabase does not perform well in the ArcGIS Hub interface. To download a pre-zipped file geodatabase, please go to https://countydataharvest.in.gov/statewide/2022/DataHarvest_2022_SingleFGDB_20230125.zip.
results.accessInformation: This data set was created as part of the Indiana Geographic Information Office's GIS Data Harvest Program. The source data used to create this dataset was provided by Indiana counties.

results.title: merriam_parcels_012425_stripped
results.description: Polygons that delineate the legally described boundaries of parcels (including right-of-way) with associated parcel attribute data from the Real Estate Tax Roll (e.g., situs address, ownership, owner address) and Appraisal Database (e.g., land use, year structure built, appraised value). The polygons cover the entire County in a seamless manner (i.e., no gaps between polygons). Coincident polygons exist to depict situations of vertical parcel ownership (e.g., condominium units, subsurface mineral rights), multiple ownership interests in a parcel (e.g., condominium common interest parcels), and leased interest in a parcel.
results.snippet: To spatially delineate the boundaries of parcels, to convey all possible ownership and leased land interest in parcels, and to make available tax and appraisal data regarding these parcels. Because of coincident polygons, extreme care must be taken when summarizing attribute data quantitatively to ensure accurate results.

results.title: 2626_baltimore_ave
results.description:
CountyParcels_DLGF_RESTRICTED is an enhanced version of County Parcel data collected from each of the 92 counties in Indiana as part of the Indiana Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI). These data include the parcel features and attributes from assessment data provided to the Department of Local Government and Finance. Please note, there may be records with duplicate parcel IDs. That will result in the DLGF information being duplicated for each record. The owner, class code, etc. will still be correct, but the value and deeded acreage fields will be for the sum of the matched numbers, not the individual polygons. IMPORTANT: All records in this dataset are completely replaced with each update. Therefore, using the "Create Layer from Selected Features" in ArcMap will not work correctly after the proceeding update, nor will definition queries based on OBJECTID.

Latest update: 11/7/2019 with 2019 polygons (GIO.COUNTY_Parcel) and 2018 pay 2019 DLGF information.

results.name: ISD_Parcels_View
results.title: ISD owned parcels
results.description:
This view contains parcel data for the City of Fort Worth and its Extra Territorial Jurisdiction (ETJ) that are owned by Public and Private Schools (primary and secondary education). A parcel is a piece of land defined by ownership. The boundaries for each parcel are defined in the legal description included in each deed conveying the property from one owner to another. This data is tracked and maintained by each county's appraisal district.

The City of Fort Worth maintains a separate but related type of record called a lot. Lots are tracked as subdivisions are initially platted and are recorded in CAD_CFWLAND. As a parcel is the portion of land that is sold, a parcel may match a lot, it may include multiple lots, or even include partial lots. The legal description for the parcel will determine which lot or lots and what portion of each is included in the parcel. Therefore, parcels will often, but not always, align with the city's lot data.

Fort Worth's parcel coverage includes all of Tarrant County as well as parcels in Denton, Johnson, Parker, and Wise Counties which fall in either the City of Fort Worth city limits or the ETJ. Full updates are performed by Fort Worth's IT Solutions department annually following the release of certified parcel data in July-August of each year. The current data is reflective of 2024 Certified data for Denton, Wise, Parker, Tarrant, and Johnson Counties. Tarrant county ownership data is updated by script nightly.

Note: Many newly divided parcels in Parker County were found to have address errors. These have been retained during the processing process for consistency with the County's certified data.

Sources:

  • Denton CAD
  • Johnson CAD
  • Parker CAD
  • Tarrant CAD
  • Wise CAD

results.title: Federally owned parcels
results.description:
This view contains parcel data for the City of Fort Worth and its Extra Territorial Jurisdiction (ETJ) that are owned by the United States Government. A parcel is a piece of land defined by ownership. The boundaries for each parcel are defined in the legal description included in each deed conveying the property from one owner to another. This data is tracked and maintained by each county's appraisal district.

The City of Fort Worth maintains a separate but related type of record called a lot. Lots are tracked as subdivisions are initially platted and are recorded in CAD_CFWLAND. As a parcel is the portion of land that is sold, a parcel may match a lot, it may include multiple lots, or even include partial lots. The legal description for the parcel will determine which lot or lots and what portion of each is included in the parcel. Therefore, parcels will often, but not always, align with the city's lot data.

Fort Worth's parcel coverage includes all of Tarrant County as well as parcels in Denton, Johnson, Parker, and Wise Counties which fall in either the City of Fort Worth city limits or the ETJ. Full updates are performed by Fort Worth's IT Solutions department annually following the release of certified parcel data in July-August of each year. The current data is reflective of 2024 Certified data for Denton, Wise, Parker, Tarrant, and Johnson Counties. Tarrant county ownership data is updated by script nightly.

Note: Many newly divided parcels in Parker County were found to have address errors. These have been retained during the processing process for consistency with the County's certified data.

Sources:

  • Denton CAD
  • Johnson CAD
  • Parker CAD
  • Tarrant CAD
  • Wise CAD
This is a view created from the Parcels Hosted Feature Service on AGOL.  It is used in the CFW Property Ownership Application.

This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

If attempting to download this data in shapefile or file geodatabase format on indianamap.org, please note that this dataset is too large to fit in a shapefile and generating a geodatabase does not perform well in the ArcGIS Hub interface. To download a pre-zipped file geodatabase, please go to https://countydataharvest.in.gov/statewide/2022/DataHarvest_2022_SingleFGDB_20230125.zip.
